description: A comprehensive study guide covering the major historical, geographical, and scientific 'firsts' in the world. This topic is highly crucial for the static general knowledge section of various competitive exams.

sections.title: First in Space Exploration
sections.description: Major historical achievements and groundbreaking milestones in the field of space and astronomy.

key_associations.associated_with: First person to go into space
key_associations.extra_info: He traveled in the Vostok 1 spacecraft in 1961, representing the Soviet Union.

key_associations.associated_with: First person to set foot on the Moon
key_associations.extra_info: He achieved this historic milestone during the Apollo 11 mission in 1969.
It was successfully launched into space by the Soviet Union in 1957.
An American engineer and entrepreneur who visited the International Space Station (ISS) in 2001.

sections.title: Geographical Discoveries and Expeditions
sections.description: The first brave explorers to reach various extreme, remote, and inaccessible locations on Earth.

important_facts.fact: The first person to successfully reach the North Pole was the American explorer Robert Peary.
The first person to successfully reach the South Pole was the Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen.
The first persons to climb Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, were Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.
The first person to lead an expedition that successfully circumnavigated the Earth by sea was Ferdinand Magellan.

sections.title: First Women in the World
sections.description: Pioneering women who reached the highest political offices, geographical peaks, and scientific milestones globally.

key_associations.extra_info: She served as the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka, taking office for the first time in 1960.
She assumed the office of the President in Argentina in 1974.
She flew on the Vostok 6 mission in 1963 for the Soviet Union.

key_associations.associated_with: First Woman to climb Mount Everest
key_associations.extra_info: A Japanese mountaineer who successfully conquered the world's highest peak in 1975.

sections.title: First in Science and Medicine
sections.description: Groundbreaking first achievements and revolutionary breakthroughs in medical science and biology.

important_facts.fact: The world's first successful human heart transplant was performed by Dr. Christiaan Barnard in South Africa.
The first vaccine ever developed was for Smallpox, created by the British physician Dr. Edward Jenner.
The world's first test-tube baby (conceived via IVF) was Louise Brown, born in the United Kingdom in 1978.
The first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell was a sheep named 'Dolly'.

sections.title: Countries and their First Records
sections.description: Countries that pioneered major administrative, sports, and civil rights milestones on a global scale.

important_facts.fact: China is the first country in the world to issue paper currency and print books.
The United States of America is the first country to draft and implement a written constitution.
New Zealand is the first country in the world to grant women the right to vote (universal suffrage) in 1893.
Greece is the first country to host the Modern Olympic Games, which were held in Athens in 1896.
Prussia (a part of modern-day Germany) was the first country in the world to make primary education compulsory.
